sceneHappening: For freedom Christ has set us free: faith working through love, and walking by the Spirit
summary: "Stand firm therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and don't be entangled again with a yoke of bondage." Paul says that if they accept circumcision, Christ will be of no benefit to them; every man who gets circumcised is obligated to do the whole law. "You are alienated from Christ, you who would be justified by the law. You have fallen away from grace." For through the Spirit, by faith, they eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness; "for in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision amounts to anything, but faith working through love." They were running well; who hindered them from obeying the truth? "A little yeast leavens the whole lump." Paul is confident in the Lord that they will take no other view, and the one who is troubling them will bear the judgment, whoever he is. If he is still preaching circumcision, why is he still persecuted? The offense of the cross has then been removed, and he wishes that those who unsettle them would go the whole way and emasculate themselves. "For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don't use your freedom for gain to the flesh, but through love be servants to one another. For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you don't consume one another." Walk by the Spirit and you will not carry out the desires of the flesh. "For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are opposed to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire." If you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. The works of the flesh are plain: sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, factions, envy, drunkenness, carousing, and the like, of which Paul warns that those who do such things will not inherit the Kingdom of God. "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law." Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts. "If we live by the Spirit, let's also walk by the Spirit. Let's not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another."
whySettingMatters: The word "flesh" (sarx) in Paul does not simply mean the body; here it is the whole self turned in on itself, with desires opposed to God. The list of the works of the flesh includes things we would expect (sexual sins, idolatry) and many that are social: strife, jealousy, rivalries, factions, envy. That fits the situation in Galatia, where the quarrel over circumcision was tearing the community apart, and 5:15 shows that the biting and devouring was already happening. The "fruit" is singular, not "fruits," and Paul presents it as the Spirit's work, not a to-do list. The statement "against such things there is no law" is a quiet way of saying that the law has nothing to condemn in a community living this way. Paul's sharp remark in 5:12 about those who "mutilate themselves" is a sarcastic wordplay on circumcision (the Greek means "cut off"), and may also allude to the priests of the goddess Cybele, who were found in Galatia and castrated themselves. Paul's "yoke of bondage" echoes how Peter described the law in Acts 15:10. The "whole law fulfilled in one word" quotes Leviticus 19:18, which Jesus also named as a great commandment.

people.note: Urges them to stand firm in freedom and walk by the Spirit.
Called to freedom, and warned against biting one another.
The ones "troubling" the Galatians who will bear judgment.
Who set us free; the cross is the offense removed by those who insist on circumcision.

questions: Paul says freedom is not a license for the flesh but a call to serve one another in love. How do freedom and service fit together?
He says the whole law is fulfilled in loving your neighbor. What does that say about what the law was for?
Several works of the flesh are relational: strife, jealousy, factions. Why might Paul include those in the list?
The fruit of the Spirit is singular. What does it say that these qualities are described as one fruit?

words.note: "For freedom Christ has set us free" (5:1, 5:13).
"Don't be entangled again with a yoke of bondage" (5:1).
"You are alienated from Christ... you have fallen away from grace" (5:4, 5:11).
"This persuasion is not from him who calls you" (5:7-8, 5:10).
"A little yeast leavens the whole lump" (5:9).
"An opportunity for the flesh" and "the works of the flesh" (5:13, 5:16-24).
"The whole law is fulfilled in one word" (5:3, 5:14, 5:18, 5:23).
